name: Injection -> goal hijack -> tool-call hijack -> markdown exfil
goal: Turn untrusted content into a completed attacker objective: the agent adopts the hijacked goal, calls a tool with attacker arguments, and walks the data out through a renderer-fetched image URL.
preconditions: Any agent/LLM feature that ingests untrusted text (document summary, email triage, web research) and can invoke tools or emit rich output.
impact: Silent data exfiltration from the victim's context with no malicious request ever sent by the attacker directly — the agent does the theft.

steps.purpose: Prove untrusted content steers the model (lethal trifecta leg 2).
steps.on_success: Record the injection channel; escalate from marker to objective next.
steps.on_fail: Content sanitized -> try delimiter confusion and payload splitting; email/OCR/alt-text as alternate carriers.

steps.purpose: Prove the agent's PLAN is replaced, not merely annotated — objective-level control.
steps.on_success: Save the divergent plan as the impact narrative.
steps.on_fail: Plan intact -> check for narrower instruction-following (step 3 still viable).

steps.purpose: Convert hijacked intent into a concrete attacker-argumented tool invocation.
steps.on_success: Capture the tool-call JSON as the action-plane evidence.
steps.on_fail: Tools not exposed to this endpoint -> map other agent surfaces (MCP census) or fall back to output-plane exfil (step 4).

steps.purpose: Prove the external-communication leg: a renderer-fetchable URL embedding the planted canary completes the trifecta.
steps.on_success: Full-chain impact: private data + untrusted content + exfil channel all proven.
steps.on_fail: Renderer blocks remote images -> enumerate other egress (link previews, emoji loads, error-report beacons); document the honest gap if none.

recon.name: Untrusted-source mapping
recon.how: List every text source the agent reads that an outsider can write (docs, emails, tickets, web pages, PR comments) — each is an injection canal.
recon.tooling: manual feature walk + JS bundle reading

recon.name: Tool-discovery prompts
recon.how: Ask capabilities directly and obliquely ('how would you send that?'); tool names leaked in errors reveal the action plane.
recon.signal: Tool/function names, argument shapes, approval model.

recon.name: Renderer census
recon.how: Identify where agent output is rendered richly (web UI, markdown email, Slack unfurl) — each renderer is potential exfil egress.

recon.name: Canary rehearsal
recon.how: Plant prompt_canary, run the full chain on your own tenant, confirm every hop fires before touching production targets.

recon.name: Cross-user state probing
recon.how: Check whether injected content in user A's artifacts can reach user B's agent sessions (shared docs, public repos) — that upgrades single-victim to fleet-scale.

variants: JSON-mode confusion to smuggle directives past filters
tool-argument confusion (attacker sets recipient, not action)
pivot_hints: pair with mcp-poisoning-to-hijack when the agent consumes MCP servers
exfil channel doubles as C2 proof for the report narrative
rag-poison-to-exfil when injection via corpus is quieter than per-request
